## Individual tasks
### Project work
I worked on Setup.R, EDA.R and Correlation.R. I created the Project.qmd as well as the index.qmd and helped fill out the group reflection along side Lara. I made sure each plot was saved as an image. Because i took care of the final presentation, i was also responsible of taking care of the repository structure.

My main task originally was to focus on the exploratory question, but near the end I took up more task. But most of my time was spent on question 1 and 3 specifically. This was complicated by the data's structure, since different countries rely on different leave schemes (e.g. par2 for the highest flat-rate payment, par3 for the highest replacement rate), each measured in its own currency, making direct comparison difficult. My initial approach, comparing scheme type and financing separately within each scheme (e.g.only the four countries relying on a fixed-rate scheme), produced no feasible results, since leave policies are fixed within a country and therefore show little to no variance over time. In the end I adopted a cross-country approach, treating each country as a single data point, which resolved the issue. 

My and Lara had a final discussion towards the end, were we each presented our results. We discussed some final thoughts: i had at first suggested selecting only specific countries for analysis (e.g. Country where voluntary maternity leave was only added later, or where it was removed). I hadn't gotten any feedback, but she had implemented it in her models at first. in the end we decided to drop it, because in my correlation check some countries were filtered out naturally. The decision to compare the different scheme (maximum duration vs. fixed rate vs. replacement rate) was a decision i made on my own. I also would have liked to compare maternity leave with paternity leave, but adding that would have been outside of our scope. 

In general i quite enjoyed working on this project, it challenged my in different ways. I had a lot of fun working on the exploratory questions, it helped my better grasp the meaning of the data set. Looking back, I think I could have experimented more. I realised too late that we were supposed to create our own package. We started the project without one, I worried adding it later would disrupt the repository structure, and since we used few functions,it didn't seem necessary at the time. Part of my hesitation was also about team coordination: I was mostly working alone, often without knowing if others were active in the repository, which made me cautious about structural changes like this. Working on a separate branch would have been safer, but I didn't have the time to set that up alongside everything else. In hindsight, using a package with roxygen documentation would have made the project much easier to structure
and explain.

I was often afraid of "ruining" the project. Working on it longer and using git more regularly showed me this fear was largely unfounded. Going forward, I'd like to be more willing to experiment, and rely more on Git as well as R's built-in functions for better reproducibility

## LLM Usage
Because i had a hard time just understanding the data, or more precisely how to work with it and interpret it, i relied a lot on LLM to explain that to me. Because i was more used to working with Claude, i only used that. The question i asked most often was like "How do i treat var XXX", "What does it mean? How do i interpret that?". This was especially relevant for the correlation analysis, as i had a hard time understanding the many NAs and how our data structure might affect the correlation measure.

When it came to coding, i am quite comfortable with tidyverse. And because i was so focused on understanding the data and being able to actually present some valuable results, i worked directly with the code. Because of that, i didn't write any functions, because i was not focused on getting a lot of plots, just a view that told a story. I did struggle with the plot presenting both mandatory and voluntary leave while comparing the absolute differences. I had a rough sketch of the plot, but i did need the helped to center the data the right way and add a vertical line and stuff.

I mostly relied on Claude to help me understand warnings and error messages and fix them. Most of them were because of typos, Claude helped me find them. Also when it came to rendering the final project.qmd there were some issues with rendering all the files, (again because of typos or not using the right lingo for Quarto), i got it fixed through using the LLM.
